reasoning.Student A:
Because the set of schools I could possibly be matched with (my Obtainable Schools) is fixed by the others' rankings and school priorities, my submitted ranking cannot change which schools are in that set. My ranking only picks the highest-ranked school among those obtainable.

Given my true preferences y > w > x > z and my high priority at y and w (priority 1 at both), the best strategy is to list schools in my true preference order so that I receive the most-preferred school that is obtainable. Listing any less-preferred school above a more-preferred obtainable school would only make my outcome worse, and listing unreachable schools higher has no benefit since they won't be assigned to me.

Therefore I rank truthfully: y first, then w, then x, then z.
